chapter: Desvigne compared; Piron, Celestin and rivals
title: Sidney Desvigne as trumpeter and leader
summary: Sidney sat in the trumpet section and never soloed but read anything and had a powerful tone; Alcorn and Phillips were the soloists.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I was gonna ask about Sidney Desvene himself.

Did he play with the band usually? Yeah, he stuck with the band from the time he organized to the time the band broke up. He always was with the band. He had four trumpets and he was one of them. He'd sit right with them. He didn't stand up in front of them. No, he never just stand up. Joe Phillip and Alvin Alcorn would do the standing. Those were solo men. Alvin Alcorn, he played out there with Kid Ur.
Yeah, I know him very well.

And he's playing here now with Papa Salastain's band. Well, Alvin Alcorn and Herman Franklin and Joe Phillip was the featured men. Sidney just played his horn. He sat there and played. He never did stand up. He sat there and played. He could read. He could read anything you put for him. He sat there and played. When he got time for the solo, either Alvin Alcorn or Joe Phillip would stand up.
Sidney never did take solo? Never did take solo. Never did solo, but he could play. How was his tone? Was it very powerful?
He had a powerful tone. You could hear him. He had good lips for blowing. Wonderful lips for blowing.
Because I don't know if I ever heard him play or not. I'm not sure I did. I talked to him in California, but never did. He had wonderful lips. I don't remember for sure if I heard that band.
He had wonderful lips for blowing. He could blow. He could blow. And you could hear him. And he sat right there and blow for you. He didn't take his horn and sit in his lap or hold it. He played.
